whatItDoes: Creates a road tax starting in fiscal year 2027–28: $4,350 per improved parcel and $2,175 per unimproved parcel each year for the first ten years. After that, a $455-per-parcel maintenance tax continues with annual inflation adjustments until repealed.
yesMeans: Approve the two-stage tax for road improvements and ongoing maintenance within the Upper Bay Permanent Road Division, with proceeds restricted to those purposes.
noMeans: Do not authorize this new road-division parcel tax.

parts.label: First ten years
parts.what: The annual rate for the first ten years is $4,350 for each improved parcel and $2,175 for each unimproved parcel, beginning in fiscal year 2027–28. The charge applies only within the Upper Bay Permanent Road Division.

parts.label: Maintenance tax continues afterward
parts.what: After the first ten years, the base charge becomes $455 per parcel per year for ongoing road maintenance. It is adjusted each July 1 with the previous calendar year’s Consumer Price Index for all urban consumers in the San Francisco–Oakland–Hayward area. The tax continues until repealed; it does not expire after ten years.

parts.label: Different official revenue descriptions
parts.what: The ballot question describes approximately $456,750 as a total for improvements. The County Counsel analysis describes that figure as annual revenue. Those official descriptions conflict; this explainer does not treat either description as a guaranteed annual collection amount.

parts.label: Restricted road spending
parts.what: Proceeds must be kept in a separate special account and used only for the measure’s stated road purposes: improvements first, then ongoing maintenance of the road within the division.

parts.label: Start and approval threshold
parts.what: The County Counsel analysis says the levy begins in the first full fiscal year after the effective date; the ballot question identifies fiscal year 2027–28. At least two-thirds of votes cast on Measure FF must be yes.
